components.text: PR #9: UIKitCSS constant + remarkable HTML status page on the kit

This PR gives extensions a standard design kit and turns remarkable's `/status` from a raw JSON dump into a **human-readable HTML page** styled with it.

- `sdk`: new public constant `UIKitCSS = "/assets/ext/v1/kit.css"` — a same-origin link any extension's HTML can load to pick up the host's design tokens/primitives. The v1 contract is **frozen-additive**: breaking changes ship at `/v2/`.
- `remarkable`: `/status` now renders an `html/template` page (kit-linked, `qk-table` of documents, ok/warn/err badges derived from `InFlight`/`GaveUp`/`LastOutcome`). The old JSON moves **unchanged** to `/status.json`.
- Template rendering auto-escapes document names (tested against `<script>` injection); zero docs shows an empty state.
- `noop` is untouched (JSON-only, not nav-linked).

**Files:** `sdk/sdk.go`, `remarkable/remarkable.go`, `remarkable/status.go`, `remarkable/status_test.go` (new), `remarkable/remarkable_test.go`.

flowchart TD
  A["GET /remarkable/status | /status.json"] --> B["statusSnapshot()"]
  B --> C{"route?"}
  C -->|"/status"| D["render statusTmpl → HTML"]
  C -->|"/status.json"| E["encode JSON (old shape)"]
  D --> F{"Badge() per doc"}
  F -->|"InFlight"| G["warn — in flight"]
  F -->|"GaveUp or failed"| H["err — gave up / failed"]
  F -->|"done"| I["ok — done"]
  F -->|"needs_input"| J["warn — needs_input"]
  F -->|"never run"| K["neutral — never run"]

components.text: **Why it matters:** extensions can now link one same-origin stylesheet and inherit the host's look with zero shared toolchain. The frozen-additive v1 guarantee means a linked page can't be silently restyled — breaking changes go to `/v2/`.

components.code:
+// UIKitCSS is the same-origin path to quack's extension design-language
+// kit: link it from any HTML an extension serves to pick up the host's
+// tokens and primitives (.qk-page, .qk-card, .qk-badge, ...) with no shared
+// toolchain. The v1 contract is frozen-additive - a breaking restyle ships
+// at /v2/, and this path keeps serving unchanged.
+const UIKitCSS = "/assets/ext/v1/kit.css"

components.text: **Why it matters:** a **path split** instead of `Accept`-header negotiation — there is exactly one consumer of each format (the SPA nav link hits `/status` HTML; tooling/noop-style polling hits `/status.json`), so negotiation buys nothing. The snapshot is factored out into `statusSnapshot()` so both handlers share one code path.

**Why it matters:** one badge function maps poller state to UI state with a deliberate priority order: `InFlight` wins over everything (a doc actively dispatching is "in flight" even if its last outcome was `done`), `GaveUp`/`failed` → err, `done` → ok, `needs_input` → warn, and **never-run stays neutral** (""), deliberately not "ok" — a doc that was never processed isn't healthy.

components.code:
+func (d statusDoc) Badge() string {
+	switch {
+	case d.InFlight:
+		return "warn"
+	case d.GaveUp, d.LastOutcome == "failed":
+		return "err"
+	case d.LastOutcome == "done":
+		return "ok"
+	case d.LastOutcome == "needs_input":
+		return "warn"
+	default:
+		return ""
+	}

components.text: **Why it matters:** doc names come from user-controlled files on the reMarkable, so rendering them into HTML is an XSS surface. `html/template`'s auto-escaping (plus a dedicated injection test) guarantees a name like `<script>alert(1)</script>` is rendered as inert text, and the `{{else}}` branch gives a friendly empty state before the first poll.

components.text: PR #892: bump dotagents pin, apply renames, drop #864 backfill

## What & why

This PR bumps the vendored **dotagents** pin (`8205969 → 3c58752`) to pick up:

- a new **`comment-authoring`** skill (reaches ACP agents automatically because `skills.paths` exposes the whole tree),
- the **`*-authoring` renames** (`write-mermaid → mermaid-authoring`, etc.).

Because dotagents now ships a root **`plugin.json`** manifest, the special-case backfill added in #864 (`dotagentsEmbeddedSkills` fallback in `acpSkillPaths` and in the skill-source test) is **dead weight** and is reverted to plain `plugin.ResolveSkillDirs` discovery.

Finally, quack's own **`skills/issue-authoring/SKILL.md`** is **deleted**: with the pin bump, dotagents also ships an `issue-authoring` skill, and two sources defining the same skill name hard-error at startup (`ErrDuplicateSkill`).

### Main files touched

- `.agents/vendor/plugins.yaml` – pin bump
- `config/quack.yaml` – three skill renames
- `internal/serve/serve.go` – remove `acpSkillPaths` backfill
- `internal/serve/skills_test.go` / `agent_skills_test.go` – updated tests
- `skills/issue-authoring/SKILL.md` – deleted
- `.agents/skills/*` – eight tracked symlinks removed
- `.agents/skills/write-tool/SKILL.md` – prose rename

components.text: PR #1012: Groundwork — agents can read artifacts

This is a purely additive groundwork PR for #1010: it wires **read paths** for chat artifacts so agents can retrieve artifacts that were already saved — before any content-moving work lands, nothing is ever unreachable. Skills and memory were already on-demand for agents; artifacts were the missing piece.

Two parallel wirings:

- **Orchestrator**: `Orchestrator.SetArtifacts` plugs the existing `artifact.Service` into its own ADK runner (`ArtifactService` on `runner.Config`) and appends ADK's stock `load_artifacts` tool (list + load). Gated by a new `load_artifacts` entry in `config/quack.yaml`'s `orchestrator.tools`, exactly like the existing `commit_memory` tool.
- **ACP agents**: a new `read_artifact` tool on the loopback MCP server. The scope (app/user/chat) is threaded `vetting.Config.Artifacts` → `buildGateNodes` in `dag/graph.go` → `MemSession` → the MCP handler, and comes **only from the registered session, never a tool argument** — so a node can never name another chat's session.
- If no artifact service exists, the tool/registration is simply skipped; no panic.

Main files: `config/quack.yaml`, `internal/acp/memorymcp.go`, `internal/dag/graph.go`, `internal/orchestrator/orchestrator.go`, `internal/serve/serve.go`, `internal/vetting/helpers.go`, plus two new end-to-end test files.

flowchart TD

  S --> O["orchestrator runner: ArtifactService set, load_artifacts tool added"]
  E["dag.Executor.artifacts"] --> G["buildGateNodes: cfg.Artifacts = artifacts"]
  G --> M["MemSession: Artifacts + AppName/UserID/ChatID from task and chatID"]
  M --> R["MCP: registerReadArtifactTool only when Artifacts is non-nil"]
  R --> T["read_artifact input: name and revision only"]
  T --> L["svc.Load scoped to the session's app/user/chat"]
  L -->|"text/* or application/json"| P["content inline"]
  L -->|"binary"| Q["content base64-encoded"]

components.text: Orchestrator artifact access is **opt-in per deployment**, gated on the `load_artifacts` string in `orchestrator.tools` — the same config-driven pattern as `commit_memory`, so deployments that don't set it are untouched.

This is the security core: `read_artifact`'s input has only `name` and optional `revision`. `AppName`/`UserID`/`SessionID` are **closure values** bound at registration time from the registered session, so a node physically cannot request another chat's artifacts — the cross-session test can only make the call fail.

components.code: +		resp, err := svc.Load(ctx, &artifact.LoadRequest{AppName: appName, UserID: userID, SessionID: chatID, FileName: args.Name, Version: args.Revision})

components.text: In `dag/graph.go`, the DAG's artifact service is pushed onto each external worker's `MemSession` together with the **task's** `AppName`/`UserID` and the run's `chatID` — never values the node supplies. This is what scopes every ACP node to its own chat.

On the orchestrator side, `SetArtifacts` does two things per run: it appends ADK's stock `loadartifactstool.New()` to the orchestrator's tool list (list + load, nothing hand-built) and sets `ArtifactService` on `runner.Config` so the runner can resolve it. A nil service means the tool is simply absent.

components.text: PR #1085: tolerate unknown frontmatter fields in builtin/vendored skills

**What changed and why.** 0.50.0 crash-looped in production and was rolled back to 0.49.2. The vendored `ponytail` plugin's `SKILL.md` gained `argument-hint` (a valid Claude Code frontmatter field) in the #1080 pin bump, but ADK's strict decoder (`decoder.KnownFields(true)`) rejects it. Worse, ADK's `fileSystemSource.ListFrontmatters` aborts its *entire* listing on the first unparseable skill - so one third-party field addition took down server startup.

The repo already had a `tolerant` wrapper that listed per-entry and skipped bad skills (used for project skills cloned from user repos), but it never applied to the builtin/vendored sources `internal/agent.Build` actually uses. This PR:

- **generalizes** `tolerant` from a real-disk-path wrapper to an `fs.FS`-backed one (`fs.ReadDir` instead of `os.ReadDir`), so it also works over the bundled `embed.FS`.
- **exports** it as `skillsource.Tolerant(src, fsys, label)`.
- **applies** it to every source in `resolvedSkillSource` and the dotagents embedded-skills fallback.

It deliberately chooses **skip-only** (log the name, keep the rest) over stripping the unknown key, because ADK's `readSkill` re-opens and re-parses the file - making ponytail fully usable would need a byte-rewriting `fs.FS` overlay, which wasn't worth it this round.

**Main files:** `internal/skillsource/skillsource.go`, `internal/serve/serve.go`, `internal/skillsource/skillsource_test.go`.

  D --> E["t.Source.LoadFrontmatter(name)"]

components.text: The boot-safety fix: every source `resolvedSkillSource` builds - the bundled `embed.FS` and each plugin skill dir - is now wrapped in `Tolerant`, so one unknown frontmatter field can never fail startup for skills that DID parse.

Generalization to any `fs.FS`: switching `os.ReadDir` to `fs.ReadDir` is what lets the same wrapper cover the embedded (non-disk) bundle, not just real directories. The `label` is stored instead of a hard `dir` path so the log still makes sense for an embedded FS.

The skip is visible, not silent: a malformed skill is logged by its label path (`filepath.Join(t.label, ...)`) with the parse error, and `warnedBadSkills` dedupes it to one line per path - so you see `field argument-hint not found in type skill.Frontmatter` instead of a crash.

components.text: PR #1129: stop the titler's answer-shaped output from becoming the chat title

The titler LLM is only ever shown the **user's first message** — but it sometimes ignored the titling instruction and returned a full multi-paragraph, markdown-decorated *answer* (QA log: `title="**Researcher Node:**\nIn a write-ahead-log (WAL) database, a checkpoint is a mechanism..."`). That raw text was persisted verbatim as the chat title. This PR adds validation and fallbacks at two layers:

- `internal/server/rest/handler.go` — tougher `titleInstruction` prompt ("do NOT answer it", plain text, one line, ≤8 words); new `sanitizeTitle` (first line only, strips `#` `*` backtick `_`, trims quotes/punctuation, caps at 8 words, returns `""` if nothing usable); new `fallbackTitle` (first ~8 words of the user's own request) used when the titler is unavailable, errors, or sanitizes to empty.
- `internal/store/store.go` — `UpdateTitle` now hard-caps every title at `MaxTitleLen` (80 runes), a single backstop for all callers (titler, fallback, manual rename, extension label).

New regression tests pin the QA log text verbatim and assert the persisted title is short and never the run's answer.

components.code:
flowchart TD
  A["runChat: first user message"] --> B[generateTitle]
  B -->|"titler nil / errored / empty"| F["fallbackTitle(user message, 8 words)"]
  B -->|"titler responded"| C[sanitizeTitle]
  C -->|"non-empty"| U[store.UpdateTitle]
  C -->|"empty"| F
  F -->|"non-empty"| U
  F -->|"empty"| X["no title set"]
  U --> T["cap at MaxTitleLen: 80 runes"]

components.text: The prompt is now blunt about the exact failure mode (#1124): a model handed a genuine question will sometimes just answer it. This is the prompt-side half of the fix — `sanitizeTitle` is the other, so neither has to be perfect alone.

components.code:
+const titleInstruction = "Generate a short chat title for the message below - do NOT answer it. " +
+	"At most 8 words, plain text, one line, no markdown (no #, *, `, quotes, or punctuation at the end)."

components.text: The core defense: whatever the titler returns is reduced to a first line with markdown stripped, quote/punctuation-trimmed, and capped at 8 words — so even a verbatim answer like the QA log's `**Researcher Node:**\nIn a write-ahead-log...` collapses to a short fragment, and an unusable response degrades to `""` instead of leaking through.

Previously a titler failure meant the chat stayed titleless forever. Now `runChat` falls back to a title derived from the user's *own request* — deliberately never from the run's answer, which is exactly how #1124's bad title would have been produced.

+			// Titler unavailable/errored/empty - never leave the chat titleless forever,
+			// and never let a later fallback reach for the run's ANSWER (#1124):
+			title = fallbackTitle(message)
+			if title == "" {
+				return
+			}

components.text: The 80-rune cap lives in the store, not in each caller: the titler, its fallback, a user's manual rename, and an extension's origin label all go through `UpdateTitle`, so one truncation covers every path instead of being duplicated (and forgotten) per call site.

components.text: PR #1140: QA mock GitHub/reMarkable backends for end-to-end flows

## What

This PR adds a **QA-mock recipe** that lets QA drive `quack:review` / `plan` / `implement` / `fix` and the reMarkable document flow against a QA server **without real GitHub App credentials or a reMarkable account**.

The actual mock servers are standalone Go tools living in `quack-extensions` (branch `qa/github-remarkable-mocks`) because the `extensions.github` / `extensions.remarkable` config blocks are opaque to core. Anything that talks to the running quack server goes through the existing `quack api` CLI.

## Why

QA previously had no way to exercise the full review pipeline (webhook → dispatch → clone → ACP → judge → artifacts) on a CI-friendly server. This PR documents the setup, ships a one-shot e2e script, and provides the webhook/GET fixtures needed for the mock to respond deterministically.

## Files touched

- `docs/qa-mocks.md` – full setup & usage guide

components.text: **`quack:review` is gated to `pull_request` labeled events only.** An `issues` "labeled" event drives `issue_plan`/`issue_implement` triggers but never review, regardless of label name. This is why the fixture is a `pull_request` event with `"action": "labeled"`.

**GET fixtures are keyed by a 16-hex-char prefix of `sha256(METHOD_PATH?QUERY)`.** A miss returns 404 with a hint instead of fabricating a response. This lets you capture new shapes once via `serve --record <real-token>` and then run fully offline.

components.code:
+GET fixtures live at `testdata/qa/github/get/<hash>.json`, keyed by
+`sha256(METHOD_PATH?QUERY)[:16 hex]` - a miss 404s with a hint instead of a
+made-up shape. To capture a new one from real GitHub once (e.g. a real PR's
+`files`/`commits`), run `serve --record <a real installation token>` and hit
+the mock the same way the extension would; the response is saved and every
+run after that is offline and credential-free.

components.text: **The e2e script polls the chat status up to 60×5s (5 min) via `quack api`** and exits with a warning if still running. Without `--chat` it simply lists chats so the operator can re-run with the new id—because quack replies 202 *before* the run/chat is created.

components.code:
+timed_out=1
+for _ in $(seq 1 60); do
+  status=$(quack api "/api/v1/chats/$chat_id" | python3 -c 'import json,sys;print(json.load(sys.stdin).get("status","?"))')
+  echo "status: $status"
+  if [ "$status" != "running" ]; then
+    timed_out=0
+    break
+  fi
+  sleep 5
+done
+[ "$timed_out" -eq 1 ] && echo "still running after 5 min - checking current state anyway"

components.text: **`deliveries.jsonl` is gitignored** because it's a runtime log the mock writes whenever quack POSTs back to GitHub. It's not a fixture—you inspect it after a run to verify what quack tried to say to GitHub.
